summary: Workflow-backed code review — one finder per correctness angle plus one finder covering all cleanup angles, an independent verifier for every distinct (file, line) location across the pooled candidates, then a ranked, capped findings report.

result.target:
SCOPE STRICTLY to git diff 345c85daa^..5581c0de1 -- round-8, the INF advisor-of-record SSOT refactor (Andrew's design). Two commits: C1 345c85daa (new front-of-chain resolver INF_A_0.aor_resolver.py + append {run-ts}-keyed event ledger + detector rewrite + A_01 comparison-emit retirement) + C2 5581c0de1 (the 14-site migration: fold census 10->1, household 4->1). IGNORE all other working-tree changes. Files center on data/inf/scripts/gold/ (INF_A_0.aor_resolver.py, lib/inflection_rep_scope.py, lib/aor_attribution_audit.py, INF_A_00/A_01, INF_B_00, INF_C_01/C_02/C_07, INF_09, INF_D_00c/d/f, INF_D_02b/c, INF_D_04, orion-gold-dispatch, tests).

CONTEXT: round-7 (9c3b4513b) false-greened because the drift monitor used a MUTABLE comparison partition keyed by the source as-of with a fixed path -- a frozen as-of collapsed two nights onto one partition (a real per-account swap went unsurfaced) and a stale label satisfied the freshness gate. Round-8 REPLACES that with Andrew's SSOT design: (a) ONE front-of-chain resolver resolves advisor_of_record exactly once (reusing the existing fold logic) and emits (i) canonical aor_resolution.parquet [the stamped field] + (ii) an APPEND event ledger at gold/dimensions/aor_ledger/events/{run-ts}.parquet -- a NEW timestamped key EVERY run, NO fixed path, uncollapsible by construction; (b) the detector ledger-diffs CHANGES only, the as-of freshness gate is DROPPED (freshness owned by the existing alarm layer: freshguard + jwt_freshness x9 + gold-freshness-guard + mdpf + comp-freshness); (c) all AoR-consuming views INHERIT the canonical field -- fold census apply_advisor_of_record_fold collapses 10->1 (the resolver), household resolve_household_advisor collapses 4->1 (C_07), ZERO per-view AoR derivation/structuring. Switch AOR_FOLD_ACTIVE is OFF and files are SERVE-HELD; the resolver-always-runs and the switch only controls resolution=servicing (OFF) vs AoR-folded (ON), so the WHOLE migration must be DELTA-0 under OFF (a pure structural refactor) and go-live is a single switch-flip.

REVIEW BAR = the go-live gate for a CLIENT-FACING advisor-attribution change. BLOCKERS (report with highest priority any NEW regression the refactor introduced): (X) any false-green / silent-pass / silent-widen in the detector or the migration -- the round-7 collapse class must be STRUCTURALLY closed and NO new silent-miss opened; (Y) the detector OR the new household RAISE aborts/blocks the nightly in NORMAL operation (a new nightly-abort regression); (Z) a placebo false-alert on a healthy day (EDGE-3 must fire value->value only); (W) a served DELTA under OFF -- the migration MUST be DELTA-0 under OFF; (V) the SSOT invariant violated -- any per-view AoR derivation/structuring surviving, or the census not truly 10->1 / 4->1.

VERIFY (ground every finding against source @ the commits):
1. UNCOLLAPSIBILITY: the ledger writes a NEW {run-ts} key per run -- confirm NO fixed/deterministic key path exists under events/ that a rerun (esp. a FROZEN as-of rerun) could overwrite; a frozen-as-of + real swap must produce two distinct keyed events, both retained. The round-7 collapse class must be structurally impossible now.
2. DETECTOR: ledger-diff CHANGES-only; as-of freshness gate DROPPED; every non-green (CANNOT-EVALUATE incl UNPARSEABLE ledger keys = writer-misbehavior) is finding-grade through the channel/SNS, NEVER a silent WARN in a try/except; exit-0 preserved (no NEW raise/abort path). Any remaining silent-false-green or silent-pass?
3. DELTA-0 UNDER OFF -- THE CRITICAL SUBTLETY DS FLAGGED, gate it hard: there are TWO inherit modes. (a) FULL attach (A_00/A_01, current-snapshot account-grain): advisor_key+rep_bucket read from the resolution; claimed 0/873 basis mismatches under OFF. (b) MOVERS-ONLY attach (apply_resolution_fold for B_00/C_01/INF_09/D_00c/D_00d/D_00f/D_02b): a pure filtered read of the resolution's is_mover rows, claimed IDENTICAL to the retired fold (under OFF zero movers -> structural no-op -> DELTA-0; under ON mover-set == fold map). VERIFY: does the FULL-vs-MOVERS-ONLY classification CORRECTLY match each consumer's frame type? A current-snapshot account-grain frame is safe for FULL; a HISTORICAL/VINTAGE frame given a FULL attach would OVERWRITE its vintage attribution with CURRENT servicing = a silent served-history DELTA under OFF (banned). Is any vintage-frame consumer mistakenly given FULL attach, or any current-snapshot consumer needlessly restricted? Is apply_resolution_fold genuinely semantically identical to the retired apply_advisor_of_record_fold (same movers, same mapping, under both switch states)?
4. SSOT CENSUS: apply_advisor_of_record_fold 10->EXACTLY-1 (resolver only); resolve_household_advisor 4->EXACTLY-1 (C_07 only, plus the conformance CHECKER which verifies-not-produces). Does test_census_single_resolution_point actually CATCH a smuggled per-view re-derivation (a real grep of the estate), or can a smuggled udf7/explicit-map/fold read slip past it? Are the RETAINED derive_advisor_key servicing derivations (C_01 rep_id map, B_00 rep_name, D_04 lifecycle) genuinely servicing-basis only, NOT AoR-structuring?
5. FLAG-2 DELTA-0: C_01 retains its 'inflection_unmapped_rep' catchall for the rep_id-unmapped-but-rep_name-resolvable subset (claimed 0/873 live) -- confirm no served-NNA delta under OFF from that subset shifting unmapped->named.
6. HOUSEHOLD: C_07 resolves once + stamps household_headline_advisor_key; C_02/D_02c/D_00d/D_04 inherit via household_headline_map. VERIFY the RAISE-on-stale-unstamped-account_team can fire ONLY in a genuinely-broken state (C_07 didn't stamp), NEVER in normal operation (else a NEW nightly-abort regression, blocker Y). hh286 = the $0 explicit-Noel account must still WIN the household headline over the 4 blank-AoR Peter accounts.
7. RESOLVER/SWITCH: resolver-always-runs; OFF -> resolution=servicing (DELTA-0), ON -> AoR-folded. Any path where OFF still changes served output? The dispatch entry is switch-gated PRE-GO (documented that GO makes it unconditional) -- confirm the PRE-GO catalogued-but-switch-gated entry does NOT run/serve under OFF.
8. Any NEW regression the 14-site migration introduced: a broken import, a dangling reference, a consumer now reading the wrong/absent column, or a test that passes vacuously.

Report a missed detector edge as a NOTE (the bar is detect+surface+don't-block+don't-silently-pass + DELTA-0-under-OFF, not provable-completeness). Ground findings against source. Switch is OFF -- rank correctness of the ACTIVE (post-GO, switch-ON) path AND the DELTA-0-under-OFF guarantee. NOTE (NOT a round-8 blocker, out of scope -- do not rank, just confirm if seen): DS flagged INF_D_02b has a LOCAL reversed rep_id map (peter<->patrick vs the canonical map) -- that is a SEPARATE pre-existing servicing-basis finding being routed independently, untouched by round-8 for DELTA-0.
result.summary: This xhigh-effort review covers the INF round-8 advisor-of-record (AoR) refactor, which moves AoR into a single SSOT resolver (INF_A_0 / aor_resolution.py) that ~10 gold consumers now inherit from. The load-bearing correctness findings cluster into four root causes: (A) the resolver stays switch-gated in dispatch while consumers call load_resolution() unconditionally, so the documented switch-only rollback either silently persists the fold or hard-aborts the nightly, and DELTA-0-under-OFF is unreachable; (C) the servicing-key basis silently flips from rep_name-slug to rep_id-primary, making DELTA-0-under-OFF (blocker W) empirical rather than structural; (B) household_headline_map now RAISES where the retired resolve_household_advisor degraded gracefully, giving household consumers new hard-abort paths; and (D) attach_advisor_key ships NaN advisor_key on any A_00-vs-resolver partition/as-of skew. The remainder are detector-completeness regressions (deleted coverage-drop detection, unparseable-key masking, cache-trust false-green, lookback aging), a resolver-write blast-radius issue, a name-allowlist SSOT test gap, and load_resolution-in-loop plus duplication/diagnostic cleanups.

findings.summary: INF_A_0 resolver is switch-gated in dispatch, but every consumer calls load_resolution() unconditionally, so the resolver-artifact coupling breaks whenever the switch is OFF while consumer code is live (post-GO rollback / any deploy skew). [same root cause also at: data/inf/scripts/gold/orion-gold-dispatch.sh:353, data/inf/scripts/gold/orion-gold-dispatch.sh:354, data/inf/scripts/gold/orion-gold-dispatch.sh:353, data/inf/scripts/gold/orion-gold-dispatch.sh:353]
findings.failure_scenario: Operator flips INF_AOR_FOLD_ACTIVE 1->0 to roll back the AoR fold. The `if ...=1` guard drops INF_A_0 from the chain, so the resolver stops rewriting aor_resolution.parquet; consumers' unconditional load_resolution() reads the LAST on-run resolution (movers still folded) and apply_resolution_fold re-keys those accounts to their AoR owner. The portal keeps showing advisor-of-record attribution AFTER the rollback meant to undo it -- a silent served DELTA that the switch-off was supposed to revert. (And if the resolution artifact is ever absent while the switch is 0 with consumer code deployed, every AoR consumer RAISEs and the whole INF nightly aborts.) The file's own comment says the entry must be made unconditional at GO, but the committed code does not implement it, contradicting the 'single switch-flip go-live / switch-only rollback reverts to servicing' contract.

findings.summary: resolve_accounts derives the OFF/servicing advisor_key via _servicing_advisor_key (rep_id-primary, rep_name fallback), replacing INF_A_00/A_01's retired derive_advisor_key(rep_name) (rep_name-slug only); for any account whose rep_id and rep_name disagree the served advisor identity changes under OFF, a served delta the refactor is required to keep at zero. [same root cause also at: data/inf/scripts/gold/INF_A_00.accounts_dimension.py:235, data/inf/scripts/gold/lib/aor_resolution.py:99, data/inf/scripts/gold/lib/aor_resolution.py:99, data/inf/scripts/gold/lib/aor_resolution.py:96]
findings.failure_scenario: An account whose rep_id maps (via _INF_SERVICING_REP_ID_MAP) to advisor A while its rep_name slugs to advisor B (the resolver's own basis_disagree ALARM population) was served advisor_key=B by the old rep_name-slug A_00; the round-8 accounts_dimension now serves advisor_key=A under OFF, silently moving that account's AUA/NNA from advisor B to advisor A on a deploy advertised as pure-structural DELTA-0. The switch never touches this - it is the servicing derivation basis itself that changed.

findings.summary: household_headline_map RAISEs on a missing stamped column, cascading to abort C_02/D_02c/D_00d/D_04 whenever account_team was not (re)stamped by C_07. [same root cause also at: data/inf/scripts/gold/lib/aor_resolution.py:323, data/inf/scripts/gold/INF_D_02c.client_directory.py:156, data/inf/scripts/gold/INF_C_02.client_performance.py:471, data/inf/scripts/gold/lib/aor_resolution.py:327]
findings.failure_scenario: If INF_C_07 is skip-gated (no rebuild) on the first round-8 nightly while a household-grain consumer rebuilds, or during an ordered/partial deploy, C_02/D_02c/D_00d/D_04 read a pre-round-8 account_team lacking household_headline_advisor_key. household_headline_map then RAISEs RuntimeError, which is uncaught in D_02c (line 156) and D_04, aborting those client-facing household gold views so they go unbuilt/stale -- a new abort path the OLD self-computing resolve_household_advisor never had.

findings.summary: A_00 loads accounts_v2 via a loader that ignores INF_AOR_ASOF while the resolver pins it, so a partition divergence ships NaN advisor_key on accounts_dimension. [same root cause also at: data/inf/scripts/gold/INF_A_00.accounts_dimension.py:236]
findings.failure_scenario: The resolver reads the INF_AOR_ASOF-pinned accounts_v2 partition, but A_00 uses load_accounts_v2_latest_healthy() which does NOT honor INF_AOR_ASOF. If a silver re-emit lands a newer healthy partition between INF_A_0 and INF_A_00 (or latest-healthy != pinned-latest for any reason), A_00's dim contains accounts absent from the resolution; attach_advisor_key only sets `mask` rows, so those accounts ship advisor_key = NaN on accounts_dimension_latest.parquet (the OLD derive-per-row path always produced a value), degrading every direct reader (A_04/C_00/C_01b/C_03/C_05). The in-code WARN itself flags this 'partition misalignment between this loader and the resolver as-of'.

findings.summary: classify_events surfaces only 'change' and 'relabel'; the round-7 COVERAGE-DROP and SOURCE-DRIFT-COVERAGE-CLIFF detectors (and their tests) are deleted, and compute_events emits NOTHING for an account present yesterday but absent from today's resolution, so a per-account coverage collapse is no longer detected here and is not re-established (the freshness layer checks partition freshness, not per-account population).
findings.failure_scenario: A roster / accounts_v2 pull silently drops a large fraction of accounts on an otherwise FRESH partition (INF advanced, so freshguard/jwt_freshness/mdpf all pass). Round-7 fired COVERAGE-DROP / SOURCE-DRIFT-COVERAGE-CLIFF; round-8's detector produces zero change/relabel events (absent accounts are silent) and greens. The shrunken advisor books reach the served portal with no alert - the exact silent-widen class the detector existed to catch, now uncovered.

findings.summary: run_resolver has no exception isolation around its non-served, rebuildable writes (event ledger line 406, state cache line 412) that run AFTER the served resolution already succeeded (line 402); since INF_A_0 is the first compute step and the dispatch aborts the whole chain on any step's non-zero exit, a transient failure on a rebuildable artifact takes down the entire INF nightly.
findings.failure_scenario: Switch ON, otherwise-healthy run: _write_parquet succeeds for RESOLUTION_KEY (line 402), then a transient S3 PutObject error hits the event-ledger write (line 406) or the LEDGER_STATE_KEY write (line 412). run_resolver wraps neither in try/except, so the exception propagates -> INF_A_0.aor_resolver.py (sys.exit(main())) exits non-zero -> orion-gold-dispatch.sh:882-889 aborts CHAIN_COMPUTE at its very first step -> INF_A_00, INF_A_01, INF_B_00, INF_C_01, INF_C_07 and every D-view never run. The served nightly is lost over an artifact this module's own docstring calls 'a CACHE, rebuildable from the event files' (and an observability event file), even though the served resolution was already written -- a new, elevated-blast-radius nightly-abort regression introduced by placing the resolver first with no write-failure isolation.

findings.summary: A single unparseable key anywhere in the ledger prefix makes the detector early-return CANNOT-EVALUATE forever, permanently masking real change/relabel drift.
findings.failure_scenario: _run_detector scans the ENTIRE prefix (not just the in-window keys) and, on any key event_key_date cannot parse, returns CANNOT-EVALUATE before ever calling classify_events. One stray/malformed .parquet in gold/dimensions/aor_ledger/events/ (a manual upload, a future writer change) converts every nightly run into a generic CANNOT-EVALUATE and never classifies the real event files, so a genuine per-account client attribution swap is never surfaced to the human -- indefinitely.

findings.summary: load_prior_state rebuilds the change-detection basis from the append-only event ledger ONLY when the state-cache READ throws (line 358); a readable-but-incomplete cache is trusted verbatim, so a real day-over-day advisor change on an account missing from that cache is silently downgraded to a non-alerting 'new' event, and the round-8 detector -- now a passive reader of resolver-emitted events, not an independent partition-differ -- greens on it.
findings.failure_scenario: The LEDGER_STATE_KEY parquet is present and readable but missing some accounts (a partial/older prior write, an out-of-band regeneration, or any cache/resolution divergence). load_prior_state returns (partial_dict, first_run=False) without invoking the events-rebuild fallback (that fires only on an exception). In compute_events an account absent from prior_state hits `prior is None` and is labeled 'new' (never alerted) even though its resolved advisor_of_record actually changed versus the true prior state. INF_D_11 only reads the events the resolver chose to emit -- unlike the round-7 detector, which independently diffed two comparison partitions and could catch the change regardless of producer correctness -- so it sees no 'change' row and prints the green 'attribution stable' message: a silent per-account attribution miss on a client-facing surface, i.e. a new false-green vector in the same class blocker X must keep structurally closed.

findings.summary: The detector's lookback window is measured from its own wall clock, so a real attribution change ages out unalerted if the detector itself is down for more than the lookback.
findings.failure_scenario: main() computes `since = now - lookback_days` (default 2) from the detector's wall clock and filters events with `event_key_date(k) >= since`. If INF_D_11 fails to run for more than 2 consecutive nights, a real per-account attribution change whose event file now predates the window is dropped from in_window and never alerted -- the human is never told of the served attribution swap (a monitor-of-the-monitor gap).

findings.summary: The SSOT census test greps only two function-call names, so a smuggled per-view AoR re-derivation via other symbols passes the gate. [same root cause also at: data/inf/scripts/gold/tests/test_aor_resolution.py:169]
findings.failure_scenario: test_census_single_resolution_point only searches for `apply_advisor_of_record_fold(` and `resolve_household_advisor(`. A future per-view edit that re-derives AoR via build_advisor_of_record_fold(), canonicalize_advisor_of_record(), a direct read of the ADVISOR_OF_RECORD_FOLD/ADVISOR_OF_RECORD_EXPLICIT globals, or _servicing_advisor_key() passes the census assertion unchanged -- so the exact per-view AoR structuring round-8 exists to eliminate can silently reappear with the gate still green (and the gate is pytest-only, not run by commit-gate).

findings.summary: load_resolution() is called inside the per-snapshot `for snap in dates` loop, dropping the load-once behavior the retired apply_advisor_of_record_fold had (module-global + _AOR_FOLD_LOADED flag). [same root cause also at: data/inf/scripts/gold/INF_D_00c.portal_leaderboard.py:451, data/inf/scripts/gold/INF_B_00.canonical_holdings.py:734]
findings.failure_scenario: A full/backfill B_00 rebuild over hundreds of snapshot dates now issues one S3 GetObject of aor_resolution.parquet per iteration instead of once per process. load_resolution() has no retry, so a single transient S3 error on any iteration RAISEs and aborts the entire multi-date rebuild partway, leaving canonical_holdings partitions partially written -- where the old self-loaded fold would have completed after one read.

findings.summary: list_event_keys (plus _s3 and load_events) re-implement helpers that already exist in lib/aor_resolution.py, from which this module already imports LEDGER_EVENTS_PREFIX.
findings.failure_scenario: aor_attribution_audit.list_event_keys (:157), _s3 (:152) and load_events (:166) duplicate aor_resolution.list_event_keys (:344), _s3 (:227) and _read_parquet. Two copies of the ledger listing/pagination/.parquet-filter logic can drift: if the writer side (aor_resolution.list_event_keys) later changes its key filter or pagination, the detector's private copy won't follow, so it enumerates a different key set than the resolver wrote and silently misses events. Import the writer's helper instead.

findings.summary: _n_absent rebuilds a second membership dict already computed by attach_advisor_key and miscounts NaN-account_id rows as absent.
findings.failure_scenario: `pd.to_numeric(dim['account_id']).map({int(a): True ...}).isna().sum()` re-derives the same account_id->present map attach_advisor_key just built (redundant O(n) work) and, because a NaN account_id coerces to NaN and maps to NaN (isna True), counts dim rows with null account_id as 'ABSENT from aor_resolution'. The WARN then over-reports the absent-account count, sending an investigator after a phantom partition-misalignment that is really just null account_ids.

refuted.summary: The resolver INF_A_0 is prepended to the chain ONLY when INF_AOR_FOLD_ACTIVE=1, but the migrated consumers (INF_A_00/A_01/C_07 + every movers-only view) unconditionally call load_resolution(), which RAISES when gold/dimensions/aor_resolution.parquet is absent; the self-sufficient per-view advisor_key derivation those scripts used to carry is deleted, so nothing produces the artifact under OFF.

Because INF_A_0 is gated on INF_AOR_FOLD_ACTIVE=1, flipping the switch OFF (the documented rollback) DROPS the resolver from the chain instead of keeping it running; the design's 'resolver always runs, OFF reverts resolution to servicing' invariant is not implemented, so the last written resolution is frozen, not reverted.
load_resolution() is called inside _filter_partition, which runs once per leaderboard window (plus each forward-walk fallback partition), re-reading the resolution from S3 every time instead of once.

classify_events computes the change-event legit-vs-bug hint with an unguarded str() on possibly-NA raw values (str(pd.NA) -> '<NA>'), unlike compute_events which NA-normalizes, so a udf7 value<->blank transition is misclassified.
Dead `if ... : pass` block in apply_resolution_fold — the conditional body is a bare pass plus a comment and does nothing.
